notes.mwasuze: Plural “you”, used for one elder out of respect.
notes.mwebale: Plural “you”, used for one elder out of respect.
notes.s39-omugenyi: A saying: guests are honoured above everyone.

guidebook.intro: Respect is at the heart of Ganda manners. Greet elders kneeling, and speak to one elder as if to many: **Mwasuze mutya?**

tips.title: Kneeling to greet
body: Women and children traditionally **fukamira** (kneel) when they greet elders, parents-in-law or important guests, and stay low until the greeting ends. Men may bow or crouch. In town it is lighter, but at home and at ceremonies it matters.

tips.title: The plural of respect
body: To one elder, use the plural “you” (**mu-**) instead of the singular (**o-** / **w-**). It is like French *vous*.

culture.title: The guest comes first
body: **Omugenyi ye mukulu**: a guest is always offered a seat and something to eat or drink, even on a short visit. Saying no outright is impolite; taste a little and say **Mwebale**.
